subject: Clarifying default lifecycle for request/response logs, prompts vs outputs
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@acme.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@clearsky.ai
Date: 2028-04-15T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Default retention question — request/response and prompt/output boundary

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. Two quick follow-ups from our compliance team: by default, what does Redwood retain from API calls made to the hosted inference endpoint? Specifically we need clarity on: 1) whether the raw prompt text is stored; 2) whether model-generated outputs are treated the same as prompts; and 3) if the request/response pair is retained together or separately.

We also need to know where retained logs live (region) and the deletion workflow for a customer-initiated purge. Can you point me to a short summary we can share with our auditors?

Thanks — Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of Ops, Acme Retail

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-15T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Default retention question — request/response and prompt/output boundary

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list. Short answer up front: by default we persist request metadata and model outputs for 30 days in the region where the customer’s account is configured; prompts (raw user-provided text) are classified separately and are only retained if a customer opts into "retain prompts" (this is off by default for hosted accounts).

Longer details and next steps below. I’ve looped in Marissa and Karthik for any legal/process nuances and to attach the retention matrix as a one-page.

What we store by default (hosted API):
- Request metadata: timestamp, route/model id, token counts, latency metrics — stored for usage and billing by default.
- Request payload (prompts): not persisted by default for hosted accounts; ephemeral in transit and used for generation unless customer enables prompt retention.
- Model outputs (responses): retained by default for 30 days for debugging, quality monitoring, and fraud mitigation — can be toggled by account setting.
- Derived artifacts (embeddings, reranking scores): retained according to the same retention policy as outputs.

Retention location and deletion flow:
- Residency: retained in the customer-configured region (us/eu/apac) unless the customer explicitly requests cross-region replication.
- Deletion: customers can request immediate purge via the Console or API; we run an expedited deletion job (aim: 72 hours) that removes artifacts from primary stores and triggers background compaction to prune backups.

I'll attach the one-pager and a sample API call you can use to request purge. If you want a SOC-friendly explanation, Marissa can add the audit log steps.

Irene
Irene Choi
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@acme.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-16T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Default retention question — request/response and prompt/output boundary

Alex — adding the auditor-friendly language here (short bullets you can paste into a control description):

- Default retention window: 30 days for request/response outputs; request bodies (prompts) are NOT retained by default on hosted accounts.
- Logical separation: prompts and outputs are treated as separate classes; outputs are persisted for diagnostics and quality signals, prompts require explicit opt-in.
- Purge process: customer calls the Delete Logs API or triggers "Purge data" in Console -> Deletion job queued -> primary shards truncated -> background compaction removes residual copies from cold stores; deletion jobs are audited and produce a job id for compliance records.
- Residency: data stored in the customer-configured region; metadata referencing deletion jobs and audit trails retained longer for compliance (90 days).

Two quick notes: 1) Dedicated/Private deployments behave differently by default — prompts may be stored locally depending on customer configuration; 2) For enterprise customers we can offer custom retention windows and an SLA for purge completion.

Attaching: redwood-log-classification-matrix.pdf (one-page) and an example purge API call.

Marissa Cole
Product Security (Data Policies), Redwood Inference

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@acme.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, security@clearsky.ai
Date: 2028-04-16T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Default retention question — request/response and prompt/output boundary

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying questions from our auditors: 
1) When you say "outputs retained for 30 days by default," are those outputs retained with the full request context (i.e., are they stored as linked pairs) or only as anonymized/result-only artifacts?
2) If a customer opts out of output retention, does any transient logging (for debugging/failure investigation) remain visible to Redwood engineers, and is that surfaced in audit logs?

We’ll need verbiage we can include in our vendor risk assessment; if you can confirm the exact wording around "linked pairs" and engineer access, that will close this out.

—Alex

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@acme.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-17T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Default retention question — request/response and prompt/output boundary

Alex — quick clarifications:

1) Linkage: outputs are stored with minimal request context (model id, timestamp, route id, and a hashed request id) by default. The raw prompt text is NOT stored unless prompt retention is enabled. That hashed request id allows us to reconstruct traces for debugging without exposing the full prompt. For audit language: "Outputs are retained with operational metadata and a non-reversible hash linking request->response; raw prompts are not retained by default."

2) Engineer access & transient logs: transient debugging logs (stack traces, error dumps) may temporarily include unpacked request/response material in ephemeral debug buffers but these are not persisted to the default retention store. Access to ephemeral debugging buffers is logged in our internal audit trail; for hosted accounts, engineers do not have persistent access to raw prompts unless the customer has enabled prompt retention or provided explicit debug consent.

If you want corporate-approved phrasing for vendor risk assessments I can send a short paragraph you can paste in — or we can schedule a 20-minute call with our security team and Clearsky if you prefer.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Inference Platform Security, Redwood Inference
